articles.title_zh: 在最近的ADF攻击中超过30人死亡
articles.content: Fear, bloodshed, and devastation have once again descended upon communities in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) stormed Cantine in the Madiwe sector of Beni territory, in the North Kivu Province during the night of Thursday, Nov. 5, into the early hours of Nov. 6, leaving civilians dead, homes burning, and an already vulnerable population gripped by terror. Justin Paluku, president of the Civil Society Forces Vives of Madiwe, confirmed that the provisional death toll stood at more than 30 civilians. “For families that went to bed hoping to wake up to another ordinary morning, the night turned into a nightmare of unimaginable suffering,” Paluku said. “We are deeply concerned about the safety of our population. Christian Civilians cannot continue living like prisoners in their own communities, constantly wondering when armed men will strike again. Our people deserve protection, peace and the freedom to live without fear.” Seeking Safety As news of the attack spread, residents began fleeing Cantine toward neighboring areas considered relatively safer. Children, women, and the elderly are among those facing the uncertainty of displacement, leaving behind homes, livelihoods, and personal belongings. For Christian survivors, the immediate concern is no longer what tomorrow will bring, but whether they will survive another attack . “We heard the sounds of violence, and fear immediately took control of us,” a survivor of the attack said. “We had no time to collect our belongings. All we wanted was to escape with our lives. We have lost our sense of security, and we do not know whether we will ever return to our homes again.” The reported burning of homes and looting of property represent more than material destruction. They strip Christian families of their dignity, deepen their vulnerability, and leave children exposed to hunger, insecurity, and psychological trauma. The wider Beni region has endured years of repeated attacks, killings, abductions, and displacement attributed to armed groups, particularly the ADF. Each new incident adds another painful chapter to the suffering of communities that continue to demand protection and justice. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . articles.title_zh: 从迫害到毕业的旅程
articles.content: On Nov. 6, Titus Hassan Malika stood with his classmates and received his diploma — a quiet but powerful moment marking the end of a long, difficult road. The Sudanese Christian, who fled violence and persecution in his homeland, had received support from International Christian Concern (ICC). With God’s help, what once seemed impossible had become reality. “The support I received from ICC is a dream come true,” Malika said. “I never imagined that someone would stand with me for so many years, believing in my future when I could barely see it myself. This graduation is not only my achievement — it is the fruit of their faithfulness and God’s provision.” Titus grew up in Sudan, where following Jesus grew increasingly dangerous . As pressure on Christian communities intensified amid conflict and targeted hostility, he was forced to leave everything behind. With little more than his faith, he crossed into Kenya as a refugee, carrying the weight of loss, uncertainty, and the hope that God still had a future for him. By His Side In 2023, ICC stepped into that uncertainty. Through consistent support, practical help, encouragement, and the means to continue his studies, we walked with Titus through years of hardship. The path was not easy. He faced the daily challenges of life, the lingering trauma of persecution, and the enduring discipline of education while far from home. Yet he pressed on. “Jesus Christ has been the center of my life from the day I fled Sudan until this moment,” he said. “When I had no home, he was my shelter. When fear tried to silence me, he gave me courage. Every step of this journey has been possible only because he walked with me and never left me alone.” As he steps into his next chapter, Titus carries both a Bachelor’s degree in business administration and management, as well as a testimony that God can bring beauty from ashes, and that the Body of Christ, when it stands with the persecuted, can help rewrite a life marked by suffering into one marked by grace. “I give thanks to God for ICC, for they have been the hands and feet of Christ to me,” he said. “As it is written, ‘And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus’ (Philippians 4:19). Truly, the Lord has done this. May he continue to bless those who have poured out their lives so that I could stand here today.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . articles.title_zh: 穆斯林枪手在高原袭击中杀死6人后没有逮捕
articles.content: Suspected Muslim Gunmen killed at least six people, including a Nigerian soldier, in separate attacks on communities in Plateau state, Nigeria. The attacks occurred on Sunday night, Nov. 8, in Bel village, Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area (LGA), and Lakas community in Panyam, near the Mangu-Pankshin border in Mangu LGA. Four people, including three civilians and a soldier, were reportedly killed when gunmen stormed Bel village at about 9 p.m. and opened fire. A resident of Bel village, Bulus Bot, who confirmed the attack to International Christian Concern (ICC), said several people also sustained gunshot injuries. The attack forced residents to seek safety as gunfire rang through the community. He said the attackers are Islamic Fulani herders who want to take over their land. Rwang Tengwong, publicity secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), confirmed the killings and identified three of the civilian victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. The soldier has not been publicly identified. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. The network of militias is responsible for four times more civilian deaths than the two prominent Islamic terror organizations, Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), combined. The study’s findings challenge the commonly held belief that the two organized terror groups kill the larger number of Christians, highlighting the Fulani network’s expanded efforts to target Christians. A Second Attack Two additional people were reportedly killed in a separate attack on the Lakas community in Panyam, bringing the reported death toll from the two incidents to at least six. “Muslim Fulani stopped us from going to the farm to harvest our crops, and we are now afraid to go to the church to worship,” Mathias said. “Nigerian authorities failed to protect us.” Tengwong told ICC that no arrests had been made following either attack. He specifically accused the Nigerian Army of failing to apprehend any of the suspected Fulani attackers. Tengwong condemned the killings and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible, warning that the failure to apprehend attackers could leave surrounding communities exposed to further violence. Residents and eyewitnesses alleged that Fulani extremists carried out the attacks, targeting predominantly Christian communities. Some residents described the assaults as part of a pattern of violence aimed at taking over ancestral lands and forcing indigenous populations from their communities. These allegations could not be independently verified. The latest attacks add to continuing reports of armed assaults against rural communities in Plateau, particularly in Barkin Ladi, Bassa, Riyom, and Mangu local government areas, where Christian farming communities have repeatedly reported killings, destruction of property, displacement, and threats to their livelihoods. articles.title_zh: 民主同盟军重返卢贝罗，在埃博拉危机中散布恐惧
articles.content: After nearly half a year away, fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have returned to Lubero territory in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). On Tuesday morning, Nov. 3, the Islamic extremist ADF attacked Maikengu village, terrorizing the community. According to local authorities, “the attackers looted homes and businesses before setting fire to houses, shops, and pharmacies. As news of the attack spread, residents began fleeing for safety. Some are heading toward Kambau and Nziapanda, leaving behind their homes and everything they worked hard to build. In this attack, one Christian was found killed with a machete alongside many others who remain untraceable.” For many families, this is another painful reminder that nowhere feels truly safe. While people are already worried about Ebola and the loss of loved ones due to this disease, they are now once again facing the fear of being killed, kidnapped, or forced to flee by Islamist terrorists. “We have already lost so much to Ebola disease, and now we are afraid of losing even more,” a woman named Jannette said. “Doctors, church leaders and local leaders are advising us to avoid crowded places, or avoid unnecessary visits, but today, with the new ADF attack, we were obliged to run for our lives. Every day, we worry about our families; we just want to live in peace and feel safe in our villages.” Renewed Trauma Maikengu is no stranger to this suffering because during the ADF’s first invasion of Bapere in June 2024, the ADF Islamist killed 42 people in many villages around it. The group’s return has reopened painful memories and renewed fears among residents who had hoped to rebuild their lives and worship God peacefully in their churches. The Congolese army has begun deploying troops to the area to stop the militants’ advance. However, for local Christians and other vulnerable civilians, the urgent need is for lasting protection, peace, and the chance to live without fear. The ADF’s return comes amid growing concerns over its activities in the region, including allegations that the group is exploiting local gold resources to finance its violence. According to a report by The Sentry , “the ADF generates approximately $1 million to $1.6 million annually from gold mines it controls in the Manguredjipa area alone, and it controls several other gold-rich territories. Abduction remains the backbone of the ADF’s manpower, supplying labor, recruits, and dependents, while reinforcing control through systematic violence.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 在这次袭击中,一名基督教徒被砍刀打死,还有许多人至今下落不明。” 对许多家庭来说,这是另一个痛苦的提醒,没有任何地方真正感到安全。 虽然人们已经担心埃博拉和由于这一疾病而失去亲人,但他们现在再次面临被伊斯兰恐怖分子杀害、绑架或被强迫逃离的恐惧。

我们只想和平地生活,在我们村庄中感到安全。” 由于民主同盟军于2024年6月第一次入侵巴佩尔,民主同盟军的伊斯兰教徒在附近许多村庄杀害了42人,所以再次遭受创伤的Maikengu并不陌生。

But unlike Adam, African preachers are refusing to stay mute. Recognizing the need for faithful interpretation of Scripture, they have drawn up a statement to help pastors stand against the idolatrous assumptions and teachings of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology. For our ongoing series of feature articles for pastors and Christian leaders, we asked Dieudonné Tamfu (PhD, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary), pastor of Église Baptiste Bethléem and Assistant Professor of Bible and Theology and Director of the Cameroon Extension Site of Bethlehem College and Seminary, to introduce readers to the recently published Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . Christian leadership is war. When God calls a man to shepherd his flock, he calls him to war against wolves. Satan, the father of lies, and his minions hate the spiritual health of God’s people, wanting nothing more than to lead the people of God from truth to idolatry. The spiritual leaders of God’s flock are called to fight against Satan’s counterfeit gospels by proclaiming the word of God (Ephesians 6:17). When those leaders fall silent, when they fail to preach the sufficiency of Christ alone, they make space for Satan to lead the people of God into idolatry. As John Calvin rightly said, “Those in authority in the church turned over to idols the office of teaching for no other reason than that they themselves were mute.” 1 The muteness of faithful leaders gives voices to idols. Since Genesis 3, the devil has been in the business of poisoning the minds of God’s people with lies. In God’s good garden, the enemy came preaching lies: If God truly loves you, he will give you the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden. Eve paid close attention while Adam idly stood by, mute. Thus he, his wife, and all his descendants died of the poison of Satan. The world is under the curse of sin because of a failure of leadership. 2 One of Satan’s most deceptive counterfeits plaguing both American and African churches is the prosperity gospel, a false teaching that elevates the idols of health, wealth, and power. David Oyedepo, a strong proponent of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology, says, “Healing is the covenant right of every child of God . . . sickness has no right to feast on your life.” He goes on to proclaim healing over his congregation: “In the name of Jesus, I decree an end to every toil with sickness and disease.” He assures them that faith in Jesus means the end of sickness. 3 As I’ve written elsewhere, this “idolatrous perversion of the gospel” turns Jesus into “a means to God’s full blessings, primarily of health, wealth, and might” in the present life. 4 Its widespread success indicates a failure on the part of so-called shepherds to engage in spiritual warfare by speaking the whole testimony of God’s word. articles.content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. " 对于我们来说,这是一个机会,可以问:‘我们该怎么办? ' 从10月31日开始到11月13日结束的青年奥林匹克运动会正在三个主办城市举行:达喀尔、迪亚姆尼亚迪奥和萨利。 活动组织者预计有近2700名14至17岁的运动员参加35个运动会,并代表200多个代表团.

该运动会吸引了一百万观众,而西部报道有超过6000名活动志愿者为所有会场配备人员. 如此多的人聚集在塞内加尔,韦斯特和他的团队集中力量为塞内加尔的教会准备福音会的机会. West说:“我们可以跑去躲起来,或者做这件事。”

“我们决定这样做。” 2026年塞内加尔达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会是非洲大陆首次举办的奥林匹克运动会. IMB Photo West是IMB在塞内加尔工作的团队领导,该部的工作集中在三个领域:福音参与、教会进步和社区发展。 青年奥林匹克运动会的外联自然符合前两个优先事项。

他说,“我们的做法是动员地方教会”。 这是他们的后院。 战略不是依赖大量国际志愿者的涌入,而是以装备当地信徒为中心,尽管有一个来自美国的志愿者团队在服役. 塞内加尔在大达喀尔地区有四所浸信会教堂。

许多代表会众的领导人以及其他部委伙伴参加了专门为奥运会设计的福音会培训。 塞内加尔的教会领袖和部委伙伴参加了一个福音会培训班,专门在达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会期间分享福音。

“开口福音对话是一个简单、非暗示性的方法。 交易纪念针是奥林匹克传统. 志愿者在达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会期间利用这些针头开始福音驱动的对话. 每个接针都配有以QR代码为特色的卡片,将人与训练有素的数字响应器相接. IMB 相片 这项工作超越了达喀尔。

articles.title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
articles.summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
articles.summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
articles.title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
articles.content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
articles.content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

articles.title: 我在這裡，請差遣我｜2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧
articles.source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
articles.summary: 2026 年 9 月 20 日，萬軍宣教年會在台中思恩堂美福教會舉行。這不只是一場禾場近況的分享，更是一個邀請：讓門徒訓練不只改變生命，也使人活出使命；從聽見遠方，到願意把自己放進神正在工作的地方。
articles.content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION・TAICHUNG 我在這裡， 請差遣我 這不只是一場禾場報告，而是一個回應的邀請：從聽見遠方，到願意把生命放進神正在工作的地方。 2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧 讓門徒訓練，不只改變生命，也使人活出使命 2026 年 9 月 20 日，我們在台中思恩堂美福教會相聚。從非洲、中東、黑海到南島，講台上的每一段分享，都不是遙遠的故事，而是正在發生的生命現場。 有人在艱難的環境裡長久陪伴，有人用教育與生活技能扶持一個家庭重新站起；也有人在受裝備之後，預備回到自己的家鄉建立教會。宣教因此不只是一趟旅程，而是一種被福音更新後的生活。 「我在這裡，請差遣我。」 宣教不是只把消息帶回來，而是讓台灣的教會看見：生命如何在長久陪伴中被建立。 從難民青年到返鄉的門徒 在生活裡接受裝備，也在生活裡預備被差遣 年會影片分享了難民青年接受一年裝備的過程：聖經、音樂、電腦、體育與生活技能一起進入每天的學習。訓練不是把信仰留在課堂，而是讓人學習承擔、服事，並在帳篷教會中實習。 當第一批學生預備回到家鄉，他們帶回去的不只是一份知識，更是一個建立教會、陪伴社區的使命。福音在這裡成為能夠走進家庭，也能夠走回故鄉的力量。 一張地圖讓遠方不再只是地名，也讓每一個禱告有了方向。 移動中的世代，也能成為被差遣的世代 把離開家鄉的路，轉化為帶著使命前行的路 在尼泊爾的分享中，青年大量前往海外工作，是家庭的盼望，也是當地教會長期面對的挑戰。好不容易建立的年輕門徒，可能很快就離開熟悉的土地。 但年會提出另一個眼光：如果門徒被健康地建立，他們不只是外出工作的人，也能在所到之處成為宣教士。流動不再只是失去，也可能成為福音跨越文化、進入新群體的道路。 ONE BODY・MANY FIELDS 四個區域，一個彼此承接的宣教身體 年會把非洲、中東、黑海與南島的工作放在同一個視野中。不同禾場有不同的語言、需要與節奏，但都指向同一件事：教會要在真實生活裡陪伴人，也要預備下一代接續前行。 非洲 難民青年裝備、社區陪伴與返鄉開拓 中東 在艱難之地以生活、產業與福音長久同行 黑海 面對變動與流離，建立能承擔使命的門徒 南島 跨越島嶼與文化，承接福音最後一棒 從聽見，到一起回應 敬拜、禱告，也讓每一個人說出自己的下一步 聚會的最後，不是停在「知道更多」。會眾一起敬拜、禱告，並在小組中分享與聆聽。有人重新看見自己的位置，有人開始為禾場守望，也有人思考：我能如何參與神已經開始的工作？ THE NEXT STEP 宣教從一個願意的回應開始 不是每一個人都立刻走到遠方，但每一個人都能開始聆聽、禱告、關心，並在神所託付的位置上踏出下一步。 認識萬軍宣教禾場 加入禱告與守望

articles.content: WANJUN FIELD UPDATE · AUGUST 2026 把進度寫清楚，也把前線安全守住 2026 年的禾場工作，不只是在地圖上增加一個點，而是讓基地、教育、生計與社區關係逐步成形。以下整理尼泊爾、寮國、烏干達、伊拉克、緬甸與東馬來西亞可公開的近況；人名、行程、證件、醫療與敏感位置不列入網站。 黑海區 尼泊爾｜工程進入收尾 道路依在地條件改採鋼筋混凝土，地下管線溝完成；大型聚會與接待空間依施工紀錄逐步整理。工程進度以現場紀錄為準，不把規劃寫成成果。 閱讀尼泊爾禾場 → 南島區 寮國｜先安頓，再發展 團隊先完成生活落腳，再評估土地、水源、雨季條件與小型農業方向。先學習文化、建立關係，才決定後續基地與生計規模。 閱讀寮國禾場 → 非洲區 烏干達｜培育連結生活技能 HOST 宣教學校持續陪伴青年，並把信仰培育、水資源、農業及小型養殖連結成可實踐的生活路徑，幫助所學能回到家庭與社區。 閱讀烏干達禾場 → 中東區 伊拉克｜基地走向長期陪伴 供水、圍護與種植條件逐步改善，團隊持續以家庭、社區及生活需要為起點，建立可長久同行、可被信任的服事。 閱讀伊拉克禾場 → 南島區 緬甸｜以教育連結家庭 學校持續以基礎教育、生活陪伴與家庭連結服事兒童；新的服務方向仍按安全、需要與在地承擔能力審慎推進。 閱讀緬甸禾場 → 南島區 東馬｜多點教育與社區陪伴 多個社區學習與陪伴據點持續運作；兒童教育、災後陪伴、家庭關懷與在地人才培育，正逐步連成一條長期路徑。 閱讀東馬禾場 → PRAY · PARTICIPATE · SUPPORT 你可以怎麼參與？ 禱告： 為在地同工、社區關係、教育與工程安全守望。 專業參與： 以教育、農業、建築、媒體或行政經驗成為長期夥伴。 奉獻支持： 讓基地、教育與生計計畫能按需要穩健推進。 資料整理至 2026 年 8 月。本文只公開可安全說明的事工方向與階段進度；未公開人名、精確位置、行程、證件、醫療、財務路線及未定案資訊。

articles.content: GOOD TV 國度新聞・非洲宣教專題 走進非洲難民中的服事——萬軍宣教工作的生命見證 透過實地拍攝、採訪與剪輯，GOOD TV 帶領觀眾走進萬軍在非洲的服事現場， 看見福音如何在艱難環境中成為盼望，也看見前方與後方同工彼此配搭的珍貴見證。 完整觀看｜GOOD TV 非洲萬軍事工精剪版 影片可直接在本頁播放 若您的瀏覽器無法顯示影片，可使用頁面下方的「前往 YouTube 觀看」按鈕。 近期，GOOD TV《國度新聞》連續播出萬軍在非洲服事的專題內容。 有了實地影像、採訪與完整剪輯，使我們能更深入地認識神所興起、所帶領的奇妙工作， 也能看見同工如何走進不同文化與艱難環境，在生命中陪伴、服事並傳遞盼望。 報導從華人宣教的整體路線出發，呈現萬軍多年來跨越地區與文化的腳步； 鏡頭也進入非洲現場，記錄宣教學校、敬拜、婦女關懷、家庭陪伴， 以及同工在日常生活中默默付出的真實樣貌。 現在正是宣教的季節。華人應當快快地起來，接棒福音使命， 在各自的崗位上彼此配搭，同心完成主所託付的工作。 從報導中看見萬軍的服事足跡 從華人出發，回應普世宣教使命 報導透過地圖整理萬軍長年累積的宣教路線。 這不只是一條地理上的移動軌跡，更代表許多同工跨越語言、文化與生活條件， 一步一步建立福音的接棒與服事平台。 透過媒體，讓更多人認識前線工作 GOOD TV 的採訪與剪輯，將分散於各地的服事內容整理成清楚的影像故事。 原本較難向外完整說明的工作，也因著新聞報導，被更多關心宣教的人看見與理解。 培育門徒，也建立同行的群體 宣教學校不只是知識與課程的傳遞，更是一段共同生活、敬拜、學習與成長的旅程。 同工在當地陪伴青年建立信仰根基，也預備他們成為能夠繼續服事別人的生命。 走進婦女與家庭，陪伴真實需要 萬軍的工作不只停留在大型聚會，而是進入家庭與日常生活。 透過婦女課程、關懷與長期陪伴，讓信仰的盼望落實在婚姻、家庭及社區關係中。 在病痛與限制中，仍然選擇留下服事 報導記錄 George 面對身體免疫系統問題與緊急就醫的經歷。 即使歷經病痛，他與妻子仍選擇留在非洲。 這份堅持不是英雄式的口號，而是在日常照顧與彼此扶持中，繼續走下去的真實信心。 崗位雖然不同，使命卻彼此相連 前方同工走進難民與社區，後方同工透過代禱、奉獻、行政與各種支持共同參與。 每一個崗位看似不同，卻都連結在同一個使命裡，成為這項工作得以持續的重要力量。 謝謝每一位同心守望與支持的同工 這個平台已經完成。感謝每一位代禱、關心、奉獻與支持萬軍的同工。 我們在這裡是一個身體、一個團隊，不分前方與後方； 願我們繼續彼此配搭，一起打這一場美好的仗。 前往 YouTube 觀看影片 ×

articles.content:
제47회 신촌포럼이 ‘듣고, 읽고, 행하자’는 주제로 서울 마포구 신촌성결교회(담임 박노훈 목사)에서 개최됐다.

이번 포럼에서는 ‘함께 읽고, 함께 듣고, 다시 오래 머무는 신앙의 여정’을 부제로 공동체 성경읽기 운동을 벌이고 있는 G&M ASIA and Japan 김승환 이사장의 주제강연과 교수들의 패널토의가 마련됐다.

박노훈 목사는 “신촌포럼은 1997년 시작돼 30년을 맞이했다. 매년 두 차례 이상 포럼을 통해 교회와 사회, 신학과 목회 사이 다리를 놓고 새로운 대안을 제시하는 일에 집중해 왔다”며 “이번 포럼은 신앙의 생활화를 제안하고 학교와 교회의 실제 적용 모델을 모색하고자 한다. 참여하는 우리 모두에게 하늘의 귀한 복이 임할 줄 믿는다”고 인사했다.

읽는 것과 듣는 것이 다른가? PRS, 아시아 41개 도시 진행

오희천 박사 사회로 신촌포럼 이상직 위원장의 포럼 소개 후, 김승환 이사장은 ‘Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture(성경을 듣고, 행하는 삶)’라는 제목으로 주제강연을 전했다.

김승환 이사장은 “성경을 읽고 들을 때 어떠한 자세와 마음으로 들어야 할지 수많은 사람들이 이야기하고 있다. 유진 피터슨 목사는 내게 필요한 말씀을 선택하고 소비하는 성향을 지적하기도 했다. 이런 ‘성경 소비자들’을 향해, 느헤미야 선지자는 백성들이 말씀에 귀를 기울였다고 전한다”며 “공동체 성경읽기는 디모데전서 4장 13절 말씀 ‘the Public Reading of Scripture’에서 왔다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “말씀이 우리를 깨우치게 하신다. 요한계시록 1장 3절 말씀에서 ‘읽는 자’는 단수형, ‘듣는 자’는 복수형으로 기록돼 있다. 훈련된 사람이 읽고, 청중들이 함께 듣는 것”이라며 “읽고 듣는 데서 끝내지 않고, 행함이 따라와야 한다. 저희 재단은 하나님께서 자라나게 하심을 믿고, 6년 전부터 교회와 신학교를 섬기기로 했다. 지금은 서울과 도쿄를 중심으로, 아시아 41개 도시에서 PRS가 진행되고 있다”고 말했다.

그는 “현재 PRS는 한국에서 서울신대가 가장 밀접하게 함께하고 있다. 고신대와 한동대, 명지학원 등 많은 단체들과 교회들이 함께하고 있다”며 “세계로도 확산되고 있다. 뉴욕을 중심으로 북미와 남미, 유럽과 중동, 아프리카 대학에서도 함께 성경을 읽고 있다. 그리고 하버드 로스쿨에서 몇 년째 모임이 이뤄지고 있다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “읽는 것과 듣는 것이 뭐가 다르냐고 하신다. 그러나 성경을 연구하듯 읽기보다(Reading), 말씀의 현재성에 주목하고자 한다”며 “지나간 글이 아니라 살아있는 말씀을 관계적으로 듣는 행위로서(Listening) 풍성함으로 초대하는 것이다. 이를 위해서는 경청의 자세와 청종이 필요하다”고 덧붙였다.

하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음 들음의 능력, 말씀으로 회복

2부 패널토의에서 ‘믿음은 들음에서 나고’라는 제목으로 오희천 교수(호서대)는 “들음은 행함을 내포한다. 한국어에서 ‘들으라’는 말에는 행하라는 의미도 함축돼 있다. 성경을 왜 들어야 하는가? 들어야 믿음이 생기기 때문”이라며 “하나님 말씀은 살아있고 생명력이 있기 때문에(히 4:12), 그리스도의 말씀(비유)은 지금 여기 생생한 삶의 현장에서 해석돼야 한다”고 말했다.

오희천 교수는 “본래 하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음은 불가분적으로 종속적이었다. 그러나 인간은 보암직도 먹음직도 한 것에 유혹돼, 들음의 능력을 상실했다. 들음의 능력을 상실한 시대는 궁핍한 시대”라며 “설교자는 시인이자 사상가로서 이런 궁핍한 시대의 전도자여야 한다. 상실된 들음의 능력은 그리스도의 말씀(레마)을 통해, 그리스도의 말씀으로 말미암아 회복된다”고 설명했다.

오 교수는 “인간이 하나님을 직접 볼 수 없듯, 하나님 말씀도 직접 들을 수 없다. 기록된 말씀을 읽어야 하나님을 볼(알) 수 있고, 기록된 말씀을 들어야 하나님 말씀(음성)을 들을 수 있다”며 “색과 소리가 너무 강하면, 영적 상상력이 약해진다. ‘무엇을 먹을까 무엇을 마실까’에 대한 관심의 색과 소리가 너무 과하면 하나님 나라와 의를 보기 어렵다. AI의 색과 소리에 너무 집착하면, 소리를 듣지 못하고 자발적으로 문명과 인공지능의 노예가 되기 쉽다”고 우려했다.

예배학적 관점 공동체 성경읽기 신·구약, 공동체 성경 읽기 증언

‘공동체 성경읽기에 대한 예배학적 관점’이라는 주제로 조기연 교수(서울신대)는 “구약 느헤미야 8장 1-10절은 이스라엘 공동체가 ‘공동체 성경읽기’를 통해 모든 백성들이 하나님 말씀을 듣고 깨달으며 하나님을 예배했다고 증언한다”며 “신약 누가복음 4장 16절 이하는 예수께서 공생애 기간 정기적으로 회당에 가셔서 예배에 참여하셨음을 증언한다. 예수께서 ‘이 글이 오늘날 너희 귀에 응했다’고 해석하신 것은 랍비의 자격을 갖추셨음을 의미한다”고 풀이했다.

조기연 교수는 “사도 시대 예배는 크게 성경봉독과 설교, 성찬으로 이뤄져 있었다. 4세기 말까지는 ‘예배의 부름’ 직후 성경봉독으로 예배가 시작됐는데, 이는 동방·서방 교회의 공통적 방식이었다”며 “4세기 안디옥 예배 전통에서는 율법서와 예언서를 읽은 후 신약의 서신서와 사도행전을 읽고, 마지막으로 복음서를 읽었다. 7세기부터는 구약과 신약 한 곳씩 읽었고, 9세기 이후 비잔틴 예전에서는 주일에 신약만 두 곳을 읽었다”고 소개했다.

조 교수는 “초대교회의 성경읽기 방식은 주로 ‘연속 읽기(lectio continua)’였으나, 점차 특정 절기에 읽어야 할 특정 본문들을 결정해서 읽는 ‘선택 읽기(lectio selecta)’로 바뀌었고, 동방·서방 교회 모두 부활절에는 사도행전을 봉독했다”며 “성 주간(Holy Week)에는 예수 그리스도의 수난을 공동체 성경읽기 형식으로 재현하고 묵상했다. 이러한 방식은 예수의 수난을 오늘 예배 공동체가 참여하고 묵상한다는 의미”라고 설명했다.

성서적 토대와 학원 사례 PRS 후 식사, 환대의 표현

‘읽어주는 사람과 듣고 지키는 사람들은 복되도다: PRS/JSU의 성서적 토대와 학원 사례를 중심으로’라는 제목으로 이승문 교수(명지전문대 교목실장)는 “공동체 성경읽기(PRS)는 초대교회 공적 낭독 구조를 현대적으로 회복하려는 실천”이라며 “PRS에서 성경을 함께 들은 직후 즉각적 해석이나 감상 나눔을 유보하는 것은 생각을 금지하기 위해서가 아니라, 본문 자체가 공동체 안에서 충분히 들리도록 시간을 확보하기 위해서”라고 전했다.

이승문 교수는 “‘Just Show Up(JSU)’은 성경이 아닌 일반 도서를 함께 읽는 실천이라는 점에서 PRS와 구별된다. PRS가 말씀의 공적 청취에 초점을 둔다면, JSU는 독서 뒤 자기표현과 상호 경청을 훈련한다”며 “PRS와 식사 제공 후 JSU를 진행하는 것은 처음 온 사람에게도 자리를 내어주고 참여 자격을 묻지 않는 환대의 표현”이라고 밝혔다.

이 교수는 “명지중학교는 청소년 PRS/JSU 그룹 모델을 이루고, 명지전문대학은 대규모 채플(PRS)과 소규모 채플(JSU), 오픈 PRS/JSU, 학과 비전모임 등 기존 교육·신앙 활동에 PRS와 JSU를 정기적으로 진행하고 있다”며 “공동체 성경읽기의 성패는 얼마나 많이 읽고 들었는가보다, 그 말씀이 삶으로 발현되는 것이 얼마나 중요한가를 알게 한다. 한 사람이 읽어주고, 공동체가 함께 듣고, 말씀을 삶에서 지킨다는 원리를 각 기관 상황에 맞게 구현해야 할 것”이라고 제언했다.

기독교 상담의 관점에서 성경 속 ‘나의 이야기’ 듣기

‘들음과 멈춤과 나눔의 미학: 기독교 상담의 관점에서 바라본 공동체 성경읽기(PRS)와 독서모임(JSU)’을 제목으로 홍정택 목사(솔트기독상담센터 대표)는 “PRS와 JSU에서 가장 주목한 것은 공동체 안에서 함께 성경을 읽고 공동체 앞에서 느낀 바를 자유롭게 이야기할 수 있도록 분위기를 제공하는 나눔의 기능”이라고 전했다.

홍정택 목사는 “JSU 독서모임이 ‘읽기→ 멈춤→ 자기언어→ 경청’의 핵심 리듬을 지향하는 점은 기존 주입식 성경공부와 다른 장점을 제공할 수 있다”며 “권위자에게 받는 일방향 교육에서 확장해 성경 이야기에 머물러 있으므로, 성경 이야기 속에서 ‘나의 이야기’를

第47届新村论坛在首尔麻浦区新村圣洁教会（主任牧师朴鲁勋）举行，主题为“聆听、阅读、践行”。本次论坛以“一起阅读、一起聆听、在信仰的旅程中再次长久停留”为副标题，安排了正在开展团体圣经阅读运动的G&M ASIA and Japan理事长金胜焕的主题演讲以及教授们的专题讨论。朴鲁勋牧师表示：“新村论坛始于1997年，如今已走过了30个年头。每年通过至少两次论坛，我们一直致力于在教会与社会、神学与牧会之间搭建桥梁，并提出新的替代方案。”他还表示：“本次论坛旨在倡导将信仰融入生活，并探索学校与教会的实际应用模式。我相信，天上宝贵的祝福将临到我们所有参与者。” 阅读和聆听有什么不同吗？

PRS在亚洲41个城市举办

在由吴熙千博士主持、新村论坛理事长李相直介绍论坛之后，金承焕理事长发表了题为“Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture（聆听圣经，践行圣经）”的主旨演讲。金胜焕理事长表示：“有很多人在谈论阅读和聆听圣经时应该以怎样的态度和心态来聆听。尤金·彼得森牧师也指出了人们倾向于选择和消费自己需要的话语。针对这些‘圣经消费者’，先知尼希米说，百姓们聆听了神的话语。”他还介绍说，“集体读经源于提摩太前书4章13节的‘the Public Reading of Scripture’（圣经的公开宣读）。”

金理事长表示：“神的话语使我们得到启迪。在启示录第1章第3节中，“念”是单数，“听”是复数。受过训练的人来朗读，听众们一起聆听。”他还表示：“不能止步于阅读和聆听，而是要付诸行动。我们基金会相信上帝会使我们成长，因此从6年前开始就决定要服侍教会和神学院。目前，PRS正在以首尔和东京为中心，在亚洲的41个城市开展。” 他说：“目前在韩国，首尔神学大学与PRS的合作最为紧密。高神大学、汉东大学、明知学园等许多团体和教会都在参与其中。”他还表示：“PRS也在向全世界传播。以纽约为中心，北美、南美、欧洲、中东和非洲的大学也在共同阅读圣经。

此外，在哈佛法学院，这样的聚会已经持续了好几年。” 金理事长表示：“有人会问，阅读和聆听有什么区别。然而，我们希望关注的是话语的当下性，而不是像研读圣经那样去阅读（Reading）。”他还补充道：“这是一种以关系性的方式聆听（Listening）活生生的话语，而不是过去的文章，从而被邀请进入丰盛的境界。为此，我们需要有倾听的态度和顺服的行动。” 神的话语与人的聆听 聆听的能力，藉着话语得着恢复

在第二部分的专题讨论中，以“信心是因听道而生”为题，湖西大学的吴熙千教授表示：“听道包含了行道。在韩语中，“听”这个词也隐含着“行”的意思。为什么我们要聆听圣经？

因为只有听了才能产生信心。”他还说：“由于神的话语是活泼有力的（来4:12），基督的话语（比喻）必须在当下、在鲜活的生活场景中得到诠释。” 吴熙千教授表示：“本来，神的话语和人的聆听是不可分割地相互依存的。然而，人类被好看又好吃的东西所诱惑，失去了聆听的能力。丧失聆听能力的时代是一个贫乏的时代。”他还表示：“传道人作为诗人兼思想家，应当成为这样一个贫乏时代的传道者。失去的聆听能力将通过基督的话语（rhema），藉着基督的话语得到恢复。” 吴教授表示：“正如人无法直接看见神一样，人也无法直接听见神的话。

只有阅读记录下来的话语，才能看见（认识）神；只有聆听记录下来的话语，才能听到神的话语（声音）。”他还表示：“如果色彩和声音过于强烈，灵性的想象力就会变弱。如果对“吃什么、喝什么”的关注所产生的色彩和声音过于强烈，就很难看到神的国和神的义。如果过于沉迷于人工智能的色彩和声音，就容易听不到声音，从而自愿成为文明和人工智能的奴隶。”

从礼拜学的角度看共同体读经 新约与旧约、共同体读经的见证

以“从礼拜学角度看待团体读经”为主题，赵基妍教授（首尔神学大学）表示：“旧约《尼希米记》第8章1-10节见证了以色列团体通过‘团体读经’让所有百姓聆听并领悟神的话语，并敬拜神。”他还表示：“新约《路加福音》第4章16节以下见证了耶稣在传道期间定期前往会堂并参与礼拜。耶稣解释说‘这段经文今天在你们耳中应验了’，这意味着他具备了拉比的资格。” 赵基妍教授表示：“使徒时代的礼拜主要由圣经朗读、讲道和圣餐组成。

直到4世纪末，“礼拜的呼召”之后，礼拜都以圣经朗读开始，这是东方和西方教会的共同做法。”他还介绍说：“在4世纪安提阿的礼拜传统中，先读律法书和先知书，然后读新约的书信和使徒行传，最后读福音书。从7世纪开始，人们分别读一段旧约和一段新约；9世纪以后，拜占庭礼仪在主日只读两段新约。”

赵教授表示：“早期教会的圣经阅读方式主要是‘连续阅读（lectio continua）’，但后来逐渐转变为‘选择阅读（lectio selecta）’，即确定在特定节期应阅读的特定经文并进行阅读。东方和西方教会都在复活节诵读《使徒行传》。这种方式意味着今天的礼拜群体参与并默想耶稣的受难。”

圣经基础和学校案例 PRS PRS 用餐后、热情好客的表达

李承文教授（明知学院牧师主任）在题为“阅读者、倾听者和坚持者有福：聚焦 PRS/JSU 的圣经基础和学院案例”的标题下说，“社区圣经阅读（PRS）是一种寻求以现代方式恢复早期教会公共阅读结构的实践。”他补充说，“在 PRS 中一起听完圣经后，不立即解释或分享欣赏的原因并不是为了禁止思考，而是因为文本本身是在社区中使用的。“这是为了确保有足够的时间让人们听到。李升文教授表示：“‘Just Show Up (JSU)’与PRS不同，它是阅读一般书籍而不是圣经的做法。

“如果说 PRS 专注于公众聆听神的话语，那么 JSU 则训练阅读后的自我表达和相互聆听，”他说。 “在 PRS 和用餐后举办 JSU 是一种热情好客的表现，为首次来访者提供空间，并且不询问参与资格。”李教授表示：“明知中学形成了青年PRS/JSU团体模式，明知学院设有大礼拜堂（PRS）和小礼拜堂（JSU），开放PRS/JSU，并举办部门愿景会议。” “除了现有的教育和宗教活动之外，PRS 和 JSU 也是定期开展的，”他说。 “社区读经的成功或失败，比读或听多少圣经更重要，而更重要的是在一个人的生活中表达出来的话语有多重要。”

他建议，要根据各机构的情况，落实一个人读、社区共同听、生活中守信用的原则。从基督徒辅导的角度聆听圣经中的“我的故事”

洪正泽牧师（Salt基督教咨询中心代表）在题为“倾听、暂停、分享的美学：从基督徒咨询的角度看社区读经（PRS）和阅读俱乐部（JSU）”的主题中说：“在PRS和JSU，我最关注的是分享功能，它提供了一种氛围，让人们可以在社区中一起阅读圣经，并在社区面前自由地谈论自己的感受。”
